title: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Ltd - 544286 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Niva Bupa FY26 GWP grew 27.4% to INR9,433 crores and IFRS PAT rose to INR366 crores; FY29 combined ratio target ~99%.
summary.overview: FY26 closed with 27.4% overall GWP growth to INR9,433 crores (retail +35%) and Ind AS PAT of INR366 crores versus INR203 crores, with ROE at 10.7%. Expense of management fell to 33.7% from 39.2%, and the IFRS combined ratio improved 160 bps to 101.4% despite a 1.1 pt rise in loss ratio. Retail market share rose to 10.1% for the full year and 10.4% in Q4. Management set a long-term IFRS combined ratio target of about 99% by FY29, which it says translates to a mid-to-high teens ROE. Commission regulation remains an open question pending regulator guidance.

financial_highlights.change: improved 160 bps; loss ratio up 1.1 pts, expense ratio down 2.7 pts
from 39.2% last year; allowable EOM ~36% incl. additional allowances
growth slowed in FY26 vs prior two years, attributed to capital raise timing
1H FY26 68.1%, 9M 66.9%; YoY deterioration ~80 bps per analyst

segments.name: Retail health
segments.commentary: FY26 retail growth 35%; H2 retail growth above 40% vs industry ~30%. Retail mix of new to renewal roughly 40:60; portfolio share 20-25%. Renewal book combined ratio ~97-98%.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Group loss ratio ~60.5% for FY26. Group split roughly one-third corporate and two-thirds Banca-based, unchanged. Analyst noted onerous-contract loss components were recognised at 9M and were unwound in Q4.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Retail bank business growing ~46% in new business per management. Asset cross-sell model viewed as de-risked under RBI guidance. Long-term policies about 20% of retail business.

guidance_outlook: Long-term IFRS combined operating ratio target of ~99% by FY29, with loss ratio flat to up 100-150 bps and savings from expense ratio, translating to a mid-to-high teens ROE (~11% currently).

Expense ratio savings expected to come from business mix shift to renewals, fixed overhead growing ~6-7% against GWP growth, and technology/Gen AI investments; management cited 2-2.5% expense benefit.
Industry retail health CAGR of 17-19% over five years, unchanged view.
Plan to take common empanelment network from 2,500 hospitals toward 5,000 in the next 4-5 months, excluding top-20 hospital groups.
Full IFRS accounts and annexures to be published on website around next week.
capex_capacity: Distribution: net addition of 58,000 agents, 50+ brokers and 23 additional financial institutions added in FY26.
Bharat strategy via own virtual agency and bank distribution into Tier 3 and below; expansion to more geographies planned in FY27.
Preferred provider network in 49 cities with 1,000+ hospitals; ~20% of claims in these cities go through them.
30+ generative AI, analytics and technology pilots or projects underway across the value chain.
Ind AS 117 (IFRS 17) effective April 2026; company goes live from the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Ticket size grew ~14-14.5% in the last six months vs first six months, driven by GST-related premium effects on both fresh and renewal business; management said all retail channels saw ticket-size growth.
Volume growth of 24% alongside 35% retail value growth; agent GWP per policy is the relevant metric per management.
Commission ratio on Indian GAAP fell sequentially due to senior citizen commission cut from 1 April 2025 and GST impact.
Management argues lower prices expand volume and value (citing GST experience) and would keep distributors remunerated if commission caps come.
Industry-wide: GST removal on retail health cited as a tailwind; Achha Kiya Insurance Liya awareness campaign is multi-year.

qa_highlights.question: What building blocks are needed to scale GWP from ~INR9,000 crores to INR15,000-16,000 crores at 25% growth, and what steady-state IFRS expense ratio is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth to come from existing multichannel distribution, product segments covering almost all income segments except poor, and Bharat/Tier 3 expansion. Long-term IFRS combined ratio target ~99% by FY29 with expense-driven savings.

qa_highlights.question: How would the company respond to potential commission caps or cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management awaits regulator guidance and prefers retaining a single expense of management limit with a possible glide path lower. It said distributors would be appropriately remunerated and volume growth would offset any impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indian GAAP expenses reverse at shareholder account?
qa_highlights.answer: Excess EOM was transferred from policyholder to shareholder account until 31 December; full-year EOM compliance led to reversal. Management called it an optical, contra-entry item with no net impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is retail claims ratio trend sustainable and what drives its improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonality from post-monsoon infections exists; plan assumes some basis-point worsening offset by operating leverage. Management said quality is improving and incidence, claim sizes are in line with plan. Renewal book combined ratio ~97-98%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are onerous contract loss components recognised, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Under IFRS, loss components are created when expected loss ratio, expenses and risk adjustment exceed 100%; a 9M loss component was unwound in Q4 and similar amounts existed in the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: How will the common empanelment and standard treatment protocols benefit the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Protocols are live for seven infections, with 144 standard treatment workflows; top-20 groups deliberately excluded in Phase 1 with the focus on mid-size hospitals to widen access. Benefits expected via care pathway and length-of-stay standardisation.

risks_watch: Commission regulation: any cap or cut on expense of management could affect distribution economics; regulator guidance awaited.
Retail loss ratio trend (66.8% FY26) and seasonal post-monsoon claims; management resists targeting a lower claims ratio.
Recognition of onerous contract loss components at group health under IFRS 17, which can swing quarterly results.
Slower AUM growth in FY26 tied to capital raise timing; management says underlying growth is steady.
Banca regulatory scrutiny (RBI); management says the bank channel is de-risked by cross-sell structure.
Industry growth normalising from the H2 GST-led surge; long-term industry retail CAGR view 17-19%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, market share and the FY29 combined-ratio path, but noticeably non-committal on commission regulation, which management deferred to the regulator. Answers on claims ratio and onerous contracts were framed defensively, with management stressing optical or accounting explanations.
key_quotes: And in Q4 specifically, we moved our market share to 10.4%, up from 9%.
So, our belief and prayers to the authority continues to be around keeping a single limit of expense of management and maybe a glide path to lower that.
That 99% combined ratio will translate to mid- to high teens ROE, which is close to 11% currently.
But this is optical only, there is a contra entry so it doesn't change anything.

adds.what: Net addition of 58,000 agents, 50+ brokers and 23 financial institutions in FY26 (distribution, already added)
Common empanelment network expansion from 2,500 to 5,000 hospitals in next 4-5 months (excluding top-20 groups)

growth.why: Management guides to IFRS combined ratio ~99% by FY29 and industry retail CAGR of 17-19%, backed by market share gains (retail 10.1% FY, 10.4% Q4), agent/broker expansion and hospital network growth to 5,000 in 4-5 months, but no explicit revenue growth guide for FY27 and no hard capacity or order numbers.
